purpose: Non-admission discovery of Japan building geometry, semantic 3D city attributes and seismic hazard context for future catastrophe exposure and hazard research; no source rights or scientific model admission.

entries.name: Japan MLIT PLATEAU municipal 3D city models (CityGML)
entries.provider: Japan Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) / municipal publishers
entries.spatial_scope: Japan; municipality-dependent coverage, not a complete national building census
entries.temporal_scope: Municipal CityGML vintages and revisions differ; exact municipality, edition and source acquisition date required
entries.resolution_or_granularity: CityGML building objects with varying LoD and optional measured height, floors, use and construction-year attributes; availability varies by city and object
entries.note: MLIT publishes open CityGML models and describes multiple permissive licence families, but exact city/edition, municipal attribution and service-specific API terms require separate review. PLATEAU's experimental CityGML API has no guaranteed stable schema or service level. LoD1 heights may be abstracted; polygon, measured height, usage and construction year are not complete, independent or insured asset records.

entries.name: Japan GSI Fundamental Geospatial Data basic items: building outlines
entries.spatial_scope: Japan; coverage and revision dates depend on mesh and production area
entries.temporal_scope: Continuously revised Fundamental Geospatial Data basic items; exact mesh file and creation date must be frozen
entries.resolution_or_granularity: JPGIS/GML basic mapping items including building exterior lines, without inferred roof type or insured valuation
entries.note: GSI requires free user registration for download and warns that Survey Act reproduction/use applications may be required. Do not automate credentialed access, mirror source bytes or assert open redistribution. Native exterior-line features are not identical to PLATEAU building objects: align vintage, map-sheet coverage, CRS and topology before any many-to-many matching.

entries.name: Japan NIED J-SHIS probabilistic seismic hazard and site amplification
entries.provider: National Research Institute for Earth Science and Disaster Resilience (NIED) / J-SHIS
entries.spatial_scope: Japan national hazard-map and subsurface grids with release-specific regional coverage
entries.temporal_scope: J-SHIS map products are released by version/scenario; preserve version, reference epoch, probability window and model assumptions
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Probabilistic shaking exceedance maps and curves (CSV/Shapefile/KML) and site amplification factors; grid and parameters differ by product
entries.note: NIED J-SHIS Terms Article 5 explicitly prohibits copying/distributing/transferring original seismic hazard maps even in a converted format; processed outputs may be distributed subject to restrictions, and commercial sale of results requires provider contact and possibly approval. Article 4 requires attribution and specific site-amplification citations. Source access stays restricted_by_terms/do_not_automate; never treat free download as licence for a public hazard raster mirror or commercial CAT model. A probability of exceedance over a specified period is not an observed event, damage, or insured loss. Exact map edition, hazard measure/horizon, mesh, data lineage and model rights still require review.
